parsed.explanation: Combined federal-national and protective division regime: national passport/visa rules force birth-sex markers and allow refusal, additional evidence, or fraud/lifetime ineligibility; entry reports confiscation and blockage. Federal facility and custody rules add identity-based exclusion, men’s placement, hormone removal, and immigration abuse. Protective division public accommodations, hate-crime, shield laws, and school protections help locally but do not override border/federal custody or documented facility bans. Adult alone faces high severity if outed at documents, government buildings, or detention. Adult with minor faces additional care/school scrutiny despite shield laws. Court challenges and legal-aid FAQ reduce certainty but not exposure. Score below 0.35, above 0.25 because no capital campaign but unremedied universal traveler-facing federal exposures.

entry_documents.exposure: National passports require sex assigned at birth; X marker eliminated for new passports. Visa/entry screening can refuse where document/presentation discrepancy or doubt exists, request evidence, and consider fraud with lifetime ineligibility. Travelers report passports confiscated or blocked and being stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid; civil-liberties lawsuit and legal-aid FAQ contest documents; several orders under litigation. Foreign advisories signal risk but offer practical notice.
entry_documents.interaction: Passport discrepancy can initiate interrogation, denial of entry or detention, linking document exposure to immigration/federal custody.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections adopted conversion-like treatment: hair cuts, hormone removal, psychiatric drugs; reports denial of care. Immigration custody reports forced labor, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse for transgender men. Arrest example: transgender student held in men’s ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime law remains; some executive orders enjoined; state/public protections exist but no documented federal detention remedy.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry refusal, facility arrest or care inquiry can move a traveler into federal/immigration custody where birth-sex/misgendered placement and medication denial operate.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order restricts government-funded single-sex facilities by birth sex. Many state/provinces ban identity-congruent facilities in government buildings, some private, four criminal; first documented capitol arrest for restroom use.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Protective division bans public-accommodation discrimination, requires gender-neutral single-user toilets, and 22 state/provinces plus DC have protections; private hotels/restaurants may be inclusive.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Division protections do not override federal/government-funded facilities or state bans; visitors can still face exclusion or trespass custody in covered spaces.

care_services.exposure: National measures threaten minors care funding/reimbursement, criminalize school staff supporting social transition, subpoena hospital records, and remove hormones in custody. Emergency care beyond facilities not fully documented.
care_services.protection: Division requires insurers cover gender-affirming care, bans conversion therapy for minors, and shield laws protect travel for care; schools have nondiscrimination policies.
care_services.interaction: A parent seeking minors care may find state shield protection, but federal rules, funding conditions, records subpoenas or emergency facility placement can re-expose the patient.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State redefines sex binary, removes gender-identity materials, directs attacks on employment protection, and names radical pro-transgender groups as counterterrorism targets; foreign advisories follow detentions. This threat framing escalates official scrutiny.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No general trans-presentational crime; hate-crime statute, employment ruling, state panic-defense repeal, and court challenges remain.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile framing can justify border/custody harshness even where local police enforce nondiscrimination.

minors_guardians.exposure: National orders criminalize teachers supporting social transition and restrict minors care funding/reimbursement; record subpoenas may expose family details. Entry/custody rules apply to minor documents and guardians.
minors_guardians.protection: Division schools protect trans students, prohibit conversion therapy, recognize families, shield laws protect care travel, and public accommodations cover service.
minors_guardians.interaction: Adult guardian may be safe locally but can become investigated if minor’s care/school identity is revealed and federal rules apply; shield laws do not document federal immunity.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented arrest and foreign detentions, but no trans-specific campaign or violence-rate. Local hostility may increase from official framing; street harassment not itemized for this division.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Division hate-crime law, panic-defense repeal, nondiscrimination; national hate-crime law; no evidence of militia/raid sweeps.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local police may respond to incidents, but federal/immigration custody and facility arrests operate under national restrictions.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Court challenges and some injunctions create uncertainty; no data on enforcement of division public accommodations or shield laws; emergency ward and nonbinary custody not documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: ACLU suit, legal-aid FAQ, equality maps, foreign advisories, existing X passports, unresolved litigation.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies may reduce but do not erase border/federal facility exposure; traveler cannot rely on unenforced state protections.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like 0.45-D, universal security screening creates continuous exposure. Lower because this regime adds passport-marker elimination, possible visa fraud/lifetime ineligibility, federal facility bans, immigration custody abuse, and state criminal facility provisions. It also has stronger local nondiscrimination than 0.45-D, but not enough to offset federal document/custody harm.

0.35-B has birth-sex hospital/custody placements with repeated abuse and inadequate remedy. This jurisdiction is worse on entry/documents and immigration custody, though better on protective division services/shield laws. Net below 0.35 because traveler can be denied entry at the border before state protections apply.

Similar to 0.25-D: compulsory birth-sex facilities, fraud pressure, no identity crime, courteous private services. Slightly higher due to protective state public accommodations, shield laws, and court remedies; lower on federal custody/border severity. Score above 0.25 but within High band.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is not safe. A traveler’s home passport is overridden by national birth-sex marker rules and visa screening, creating border exposure before any state protection can apply. If presentation differs from assigned sex, officers can demand evidence, refuse entry, or pursue fraud; reports show confiscation and strandings. Once in country, federal government-funded facilities and many state bans can force exclusion, and arrest can lead to men’s custody and hormone removal. The protective division offers public accommodations, hate-crime, school and care-shield protections, useful for hotels, clinics and families, but the dossier does not document federal pre-emption or effective remedy for border/custody. For adult alone and parent with minor, severity after outing is high.
